question: does the band-envelope horizon result survive a real EMG control
dataset: Sleep-EDF sleep-cassette, EEG Fpz-Cz + EMG submental
envelope: strictly causal: one-directional bandpass, rectify, causal low-pass
span: sliced to the scored sleep period (+/- 10 min), NOT from file start; these recordings begin hours before lights-out and a from-start slice is ~100% wake
residualisation: EEG envelope regressed on concurrent + 8 lags of BOTH the EMG tone channel and the EOG envelope, per subject; concurrent inclusion makes this conservative
emg_note: EMG submental is stored at 1 Hz in sleep-cassette and upsampled by the reader. It is used unfiltered as a muscle-tone regressor; band-passing it would filter interpolation artifact, not muscle.
